theme: Moses’ final blessing; his death, the prophet yet to come
readingInstruction: Read Deuteronomy 33:1-34:12. This is the end of the Pentateuch. Moses blesses the tribes and then climbs Mount Nebo to die. Read the last chapter slowly, and notice the final description of Moses.
settingTheScene: This is the last day in the five books of Moses. Before he dies, Moses speaks a blessing over each of the tribes, much as Jacob did at the end of Genesis. Then the narrator describes his death on Mount Nebo, his burial, and a verdict on his life. The close of the book sets up the transition to Joshua and the conquest, but also leaves a hopeful question hanging: where is the prophet like Moses who is yet to come?
observation: “The LORD came from Sinai and dawned from Seir upon us; he shone forth from Mount Paran” (33:2).
“Yes, he loved his people… and they followed in your steps, receiving direction from you” (33:3).
Moses blesses the tribes, including Judah: “Hear, O LORD, the voice of Judah” (33:7), and Levi, who is to teach Jacob God’s rules and offer incense (33:8-11).
“The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms” (33:27).
“Happy are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD, the shield of your help, and the sword of your triumph?” (33:29).
Moses goes up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, and the LORD shows him all the land (34:1-4).
“So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD” (34:5).
“And there has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face” (34:10).
interpretation:
The blessing of the tribes shows Moses as a father and a pastor to the end. His last words are not rebuke but blessing. After forty years of leading a difficult people, his final act is to bless them, one tribe after another. A good leader leaves the people with a benediction.

The most famous verse is 33:27: “The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms.” It is a fitting summary of Moses’ message. God is the home of his people, as Psalm 90 said at the start of this unit. And underneath are the everlasting arms, a picture of unseen support. When we fall, we fall into the hands of God.

The death of Moses is told with beautiful restraint. He climbs the mountain, sees the land, and dies “according to the word of the LORD.” The Hebrew can also mean “by the mouth of the LORD,” and the rabbis said he died by a kiss. He is buried by God himself, and “no one knows the place of his burial to this day.” There is no tomb to venerate. He was not worshiped, and God made sure that no one would turn his grave into a shrine.

The last paragraph is the verdict. Moses was 120 years old, with unimpaired eyesight and vigor. The people wept for thirty days. And then comes the line that looks forward: “There has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.” It is a statement of Moses’ greatness, and it also leaves a longing. God had promised another prophet like Moses (18:15). The Pentateuch ends by saying that he has not yet come.

This is why the end of Deuteronomy is not an ending. It is a pause in a larger story. The Law has done its work. It has described the covenant, shown Israel’s need, and pointed forward. The rest of the Bible waits for someone greater than Moses.
connection: Hebrews 3:5-6 says that Moses was faithful “as a servant in all God’s house,” but Christ is faithful “as a son over God’s house.” Jude 9 mentions a dispute about the body of Moses. At the transfiguration, Moses appears with Jesus and talks with him about his departure (Luke 9:30-31). John 1:17 says, “The law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.” The everlasting arms are now the arms of Christ, who took the children in his arms and blessed them (Mark 10:16).
application:
Spend time with the verse “The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms.” Where do you need to feel them?

Think about how you want to finish your own life of service. Is there a blessing you want to leave?

Thank God for Moses, and for the one who is greater than Moses.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that underneath you are his everlasting arms.
Thank him for Jesus, the greater prophet.
Ask him to teach you to finish well and leave a legacy of faith.
